answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to grow a verifiable orchard of past work before it earns trust: every completed job leaves a signed receipt on a public ledger, and reputation is that accumulated, checkable history, not a self-declared profile. Newcomers start at the horizon of trust, limited to small bonded tasks, and climb only as independent verifiers confirm their work. A fake identity is cheap, but forging a mesa of consistent verified receipts is expensive: each fake must post bonds, do real work, and survive audits.
